newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo platinum, palladium rise sharply.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo platinum, palladium rise sharply.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo platinum and palladium futures ended sharply higher across the board on Wednesday, buoyed by strong bullion prices and the yen's further drop against the dollar, traders said.
The four distant months surged by the 22 yen per gram daily limit during the day. The benchmark December contract was up 19 yen at 543 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from 12 yen to 17 yen per gram higher, with most-active benchmark December ending up 16 yen at 1,382 yen.

"Backed by the deadlocked Japan-Russia talks of platinum group metals and the yen's further drop, heavy short-covering by individual investors lifted palladium futures," one trader said. A lack of sellers in the market also helped boost prices, he said.
Platinum futures rose on the heels of palladium.
Traders said the bulk of the short-positions in palladium futures were still held by individual investors, indicating that palladium futures have more room to rise.
Most gold futures ended marginally firmer, as price rises were limited by a continuing fall in bullion prices.
Bullion edged down to $337.30/60 per ounce at 0758 GMT, against $339.80/340.30 in New York on Tuesday.
In the bullion market, overseas selling pressure overwhelmed some buying by trade houses in arbitrage dealings.
"In the continued bearish sentiment, producers, who had waiting for prices to rebound, have appeared to rush to sell gold for heading purposes," one trader said.
Gold futures ranged from four yen per gram lower to six yen firmer. Most-active benchmark December was flat at 1,337 yen.
Silver futures were weaker. Benchmark December silver was off 1.4 yen per 10 grams at 194.2 yen.
